narrative: The model estimates a 64% chance that you will leave your job, so it treats leaving as more likely than staying. On that basis, the promotion decision is being treated as risky until retention concerns are addressed. The strongest driver is that you reported having other job opportunities; this pushes the prediction toward leaving, and it matters because only about a quarter of employees predicted to stay had such opportunities. The second driver is your difficult work-life balance, which also pushes toward leaving and stands out because difficult balance was reported by only about one in ten employees predicted to stay. Third is your 6–10 years of overall experience; this band also increased the leaving signal, even though it is common among employees predicted to stay. To change this picture, the organization should discuss concrete retention steps—internal career paths, promotion timing, flexibility, and workload support—and you should clarify your commitment and what would make the role sustainable. A promotion may be reconsidered once the leave risk is reduced.
